task: Ops safety: teardown-all snapshot gate + dependents gate (CRIT-01); frontend build passes the API Gateway URL, fails on empty values, uses pipefail (HIGH-07, LOW-18); .dockerignore for both images (MED-16)

context.why: From the 2026-09-28 repo audit (_docs/audits/2026-09-28-kiro-repo-audit.json). teardown-all deletes the RDS instance while skipping the final snapshot, with no check that a recent snapshot exists and no check that dependent stacks were really deleted. bin/frontend/build never passes REACT_APP_API_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT_URL, so the bundle bakes 'undefined' into the avatar upload URL, and without pipefail a failed ECR login does not stop the script.
context.snapshot_gate: Runs immediately after the DELETE confirmation, before any stack is deleted. If the RDS instance does not exist, the gate is skipped. If the instance exists, it finds the newest AVAILABLE manual snapshot of cruddur-crddb-instance. If that snapshot is at most 90 minutes old, it proceeds. Otherwise it asks the operator to type SNAPSHOT, then creates cruddur-crddb-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-teardown and waits until it is available. Any AWS error (for example an expired SSO session) exits before anything is deleted. It then compares the snapshot with DBSnapshotIdentifier in aws/cfn/db/config.toml and prints a WARNING (not a stop) on mismatch; the warning is repeated at the end of the script.
context.dependents_gate: Runs after the CrdService delete and before the CrdDb/RDS section. If describe-stacks for CrdAuth, CrdFrontend or CrdService returns anything other than 'does not exist', the script exits 1 before touching RDS, CrdDb, CrdCluster or CrdNet.
context.tested: Claude applied these exact edits to a reconstruction of both scripts and ran them against a stubbed aws CLI. Seven teardown scenarios were run: no instance, fresh snapshot, stale snapshot declined, stale snapshot accepted, no snapshot, expired SSO, and CrdService stuck in DELETE_FAILED. Every scenario did the right thing, and zero delete calls were made in the three abort cases. For the build, a failed ECR login stopped the script before the push, and an empty CLIENT_ID aborted it.
context.edit_method: Every change below is an exact find-and-replace: 'old' must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the file and is replaced by 'new'. Whitespace, backslashes and backticks are significant. Use the IDE file-edit tool.

phases.name: Read before writing (STOP conditions)
actions: Run: GIT_PAGER=cat git status --short (expect no output) and git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD (expect '0	0'). If either differs, STOP and report.
Read bin/cfn/teardown-all and bin/frontend/build in full.

For each edit in phases 2 and 3, confirm its 'old' string occurs exactly once in the named file. If any occurs zero times or more than once, STOP and report which one and what the file actually contains there.
Confirm neither frontend-react-js/.dockerignore nor backend-flask/.dockerignore exists. If either exists, STOP and paste its content.

Read every Dockerfile* in frontend-react-js/ and backend-flask/, and the build: sections of docker-compose.yml. STOP and report if any COPY or ADD source path is node_modules, build, .env*, __pycache__ or .pytest_cache. NOTE: 'COPY --from=build' in frontend-react-js/Dockerfile.prod refers to the build STAGE, not a path, and is expected; do not stop for it.

edits.id: TD-A snapshot gate (after the DELETE confirmation)
edits.new:
if [ "$CONFIRM" != "DELETE" ]; then
  echo "Aborted."
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- snapshot gate
# Audit CRIT-01. The RDS delete further down skips the final snapshot, so any
# write made after the newest manual snapshot would be lost for good. Before
# deleting ANYTHING, require an available manual snapshot of this instance that
# is at most MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MIN minutes old, or offer to take one now. Every
# failure in this block exits before a single stack is touched.
MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MIN=90
DB_CONFIG="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../../aws/cfn/db/config.toml"
SNAP_ID=""
POINTER_WARNING=""

echo "--- Snapshot gate ---"
INSTANCE_OUT=$(aws rds describe-db-instances \
  --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
  --region "$REGION" \
  --query 'DBInstances[0].DBInstanceStatus' \
  --output text 2>&1)
INSTANCE_RC=$?

if [ $INSTANCE_RC -ne 0 ]; then
  if echo "$INSTANCE_OUT" | grep -q "DBInstanceNotFound"; then
    echo "RDS instance ${DB_INSTANCE} does not exist; nothing to protect. Gate skipped."
  else
    echo "ERROR: could not check the RDS instance (expired SSO session?):" >&2
    echo "$INSTANCE_OUT" >&2
    echo "Nothing has been deleted." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  LATEST=$(aws rds describe-db-snapshots \
    --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
    --snapshot-type manual \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --query 'reverse(sort_by(DBSnapshots[?Status==`available`], &SnapshotCreateTime))[0].[DBSnapshotIdentifier,SnapshotCreateTime]' \
    --output text 2>&1)
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: could not list snapshots:" >&2
    echo "$LATEST" >&2
    echo "Nothing has been deleted." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  LATEST_ID=$(echo "$LATEST" | awk '{print $1}')
  LATEST_TIME=$(echo "$LATEST" | awk '{print $2}')
  AGE_MIN=""
  if [ -n "$LATEST_ID" ] && [ "$LATEST_ID" != "None" ]; then
    LATEST_EPOCH=$(date -u -d "$LATEST_TIME" +%s 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$LATEST_EPOCH" ]; then
      AGE_MIN=$(( ( $(date -u +%s) - LATEST_EPOCH ) / 60 ))
      echo "Newest available manual snapshot: ${LATEST_ID} (${AGE_MIN} min old)"
    else
      echo "Newest manual snapshot ${LATEST_ID} has an unreadable timestamp: ${LATEST_TIME}"
    fi
  else
    echo "No available manual snapshot of ${DB_INSTANCE} was found."
  fi

  if [ -n "$AGE_MIN" ] && [ "$AGE_MIN" -le "$MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MIN" ]; then
    SNAP_ID="$LATEST_ID"
    echo "Recent enough (limit ${MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MIN} min). Proceeding."
  else
    NEW_SNAP="cruddur-crddb-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d-%H%M)-teardown"
    echo "No snapshot from the last ${MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MIN} minutes."
    read -p "Type SNAPSHOT to create ${NEW_SNAP} now (anything else aborts): " SNAP_CONFIRM
    if [ "$SNAP_CONFIRM" != "SNAPSHOT" ]; then
      echo "Aborted. Nothing has been deleted."
      exit 1
    fi
    if ! aws rds create-db-snapshot \
      --db-instance-identifier "$DB_INSTANCE" \
      --db-snapshot-identifier "$NEW_SNAP" \
      --region "$REGION" \
      --query 'DBSnapshot.DBSnapshotIdentifier' \
      --output text; then
      echo "ERROR: create-db-snapshot failed. Nothing has been deleted." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "Waiting for ${NEW_SNAP} to become available (usually 2-5 minutes)..."
    if ! aws rds wait db-snapshot-available \
      --db-snapshot-identifier "$NEW_SNAP" \
      --region "$REGION"; then
      echo "ERROR: ${NEW_SNAP} did not become available. Nothing has been deleted." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    SNAP_ID="$NEW_SNAP"
    echo "Snapshot ${SNAP_ID} is available."
  fi

  # The next deploy restores whatever config.toml names. Warn (do not stop) if
  # it is not the snapshot protecting this teardown: the data is safe either
  # way, but deploying from an older pointer would silently roll it back.
  CONFIG_SNAP=$(grep DBSnapshotIdentifier "$DB_CONFIG" 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'cruddur-crddb-[A-Za-z0-9-]*' | head -1)
  if [ "$CONFIG_SNAP" = "$SNAP_ID" ]; then
    echo "aws/cfn/db/config.toml already points at ${SNAP_ID}."
  else
    POINTER_WARNING="WARNING: aws/cfn/db/config.toml points at '${CONFIG_SNAP:-<not found>}', not '${SNAP_ID}'. Repoint it before the next deploy, or that deploy restores OLDER data."
    echo "$POINTER_WARNING"
  fi
fi

edits.id: TD-B dependents gate (before the CrdDb section)
edits.new:
delete_stack CrdService

# -------------------------------------------------------------- dependents gate
# Audit CRIT-01, part 2. delete_stack only prints a message when a delete fails
# (there is no set -e), so a stuck CrdAuth, CrdFrontend or CrdService would fall
# straight through to the RDS delete while stacks that import CrdDb exports
# still exist. Any answer other than "does not exist" (an expired SSO session
# included) counts as still present: fail safe.
echo "--- Dependents gate: CrdAuth, CrdFrontend and CrdService must be gone ---"
STILL_PRESENT=0
for s in CrdAuth CrdFrontend CrdService; do
  OUT=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name "$s" --region "$REGION" \
    --query 'Stacks[0].StackStatus' --output text 2>&1)
  if echo "$OUT" | grep -q "does not exist"; then
    echo "  ${s}: gone"
  else
    echo "  ${s}: STILL PRESENT (${OUT})" >&2
    STILL_PRESENT=1
  fi
done
if [ "$STILL_PRESENT" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: a dependent stack still exists. The RDS instance, CrdDb, CrdCluster" >&2
  echo "and CrdNet were NOT touched. Fix that stack in the console, then re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 3) CrdDb

edits.new:

echo "Snapshot protecting this teardown: ${SNAP_ID:-none (no RDS instance existed at start)}"
if [ -n "$POINTER_WARNING" ]; then

fi

edits.id: FB-B API Gateway value + empty-value guard
edits.new:
CLIENT_ID="12va2n69rq2of98ivm60b9625v"

# ========================================
# API GATEWAY (avatar upload)
# ========================================
# Audit HIGH-07: without this build-arg the bundle bakes "undefined" into the
# avatar upload URL (ProfileForm.js). Public value: it ships to every browser.
API_GATEWAY_URL="https://rtvb6kbife.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"

# An empty REACT_APP_* value does not fail the build; it silently produces a
# broken bundle. Refuse to build instead.
for v in BACKEND_URL AWS_REGION USER_POOL_ID CLIENT_ID API_GATEWAY_URL; do
  if [ -z "${!v}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: required build value ${v} is empty. Aborting." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# `COPY . .`; without this file the host's node_modules and a stale build/
# would be copied over the clean install.
node_modules
build
.env
.env.*
npm-debug.log*

# Build context hygiene (audit MED-16). Dockerfile.prod runs `COPY . .`;
# keep local bytecode caches and env files out of the image.
**/__pycache__
**/*.pyc
.pytest_cache
.env
.env.*

phases.name: Report
actions: Paste the raw output of every phase-5 command.
Report the phase-1 findings: the build contexts in docker-compose.yml and any Dockerfile COPY/ADD lines you inspected.
State any deviation from this spec and why. If any gate did not match, say so plainly. Do not report a pass you did not observe.
State explicitly that you ran no AWS command, no docker command, and did not execute bin/cfn/teardown-all or bin/frontend/build.

must_not: Do not run git add, git commit, git push, or any history-rewriting command. The operator commits.
Do not EXECUTE bin/cfn/teardown-all or bin/frontend/build under any circumstances, not even with stubs. bash -n (syntax check only) is the only permitted invocation.
Do not run any aws command or any docker command.
Do not write files via shell redirection, python, sed, or any command. Use the IDE file-edit tool so the operator sees each diff.
Do not modify any file other than bin/cfn/teardown-all and bin/frontend/build, and do not create any file other than the two .dockerignore files.
Do not change --skip-final-snapshot, the existing RDS delete/wait logic, the stack deletion order, or the Cognito/backend values in bin/frontend/build.
Do not 'improve' the edits (no extra quoting, no set -u, no refactors). Report suggestions instead.
Do not invent content if a phase-1 check fails; stop and report.
